turn.context: Four steps; nothing changes for staff until step 3, so steps 1 and 2 are muted. The exit at step 2 is the load-bearing offer. Discharge before bed mapping, because the files make it a prerequisite.

transcript.label: Transcript turn 31 · What a first step looks like

text: There are four steps. Your day does not change until the third one.
bullets: Step 1 is read access. Your IT team connects us to the systems you already run. About two weeks.
Step 2 is measuring what happens now. Four weeks of real numbers, and nobody works differently.
Step 3 is where the day changes. Step 4 is the build: discharge first, then the bed mapping on top.
chat.pointer: Pick a step to open it. The doors at the end lead into how it is built and how the day changes.
chat.invite: At the end of step 2 you have your own dead bed time, not our guess. To start we need read access from IT, and one name from you.
chat.note: You find out if we were wrong before you spend anything.
prompts: Who should own this until the managers are in?
Can we skip straight to step 3?
